You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From ecb6237fa397b7b810d798ad19322eca466dbab1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jun 2022 11:30:37 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] x86/xen: Remove undefined behavior in setup_features()

1 << 31 is undefined. So switch to 1U << 31.

Fixes: 5ead97c84fa7 ("xen: Core Xen implementation")
Signed-off-by: Julien Grall <jgrall@amazon.com>
Reviewed-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220617103037.57828-1-julien@xen.org
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>

diff --git a/drivers/xen/features.c b/drivers/xen/features.c
index 7b591443833c..87f1828d40d5 100644
--- a/drivers/xen/features.c
+++ b/drivers/xen/features.c
@@ -42,7 +42,7 @@ void xen_setup_features(void)
 		if (HYPERVISOR_xen_version(XENVER_get_features, &fi) < 0)
 			break;
 		for (j = 0; j < 32; j++)
-			xen_features[i * 32 + j] = !!(fi.submap & 1<<j);
+			xen_features[i * 32 + j] = !!(fi.submap & 1U << j);
 	}
 
 	if (xen_pv_domain()) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/xen/features.c`**
- The line of code that previously used `1 << 31` has been modified to `1U << 31`. This change ensures that the operation does not invoke undefined behavior, as shifting a signed integer can lead to issues when the shift exceeds the bit-width of the type.

### Relationships
- The modification in `features.c` directly addresses a potential bug related to undefined behavior in the original implementation. The change is a straightforward fix that enhances the robustness of the code by using an unsigned integer for the shift operation, thereby preventing any unintended consequences that could arise from using a signed integer. This patch is linked to a previous commit identified by the hash `5ead97c84fa7`, which introduced the original code that contained the issue.

        The use of `1 << 31` in the code can lead to undefined behavior because shifting a signed integer left by more than or equal to the number of bits in the type (in this case, 32 bits for a 32-bit integer) is not defined by the C standard. This can result in unexpected behavior or program crashes, especially on platforms where the behavior is not well-defined. By changing it to `1U << 31`, the code now uses an unsigned integer, which avoids this issue.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
1 << 31
```
Reason:
The expression `1 << 31` involves shifting a signed integer (1) left by 31 bits. According to the C standard, shifting a signed integer left by a number of bits equal to or greater than the width of the type (32 bits for a 32-bit integer) results in undefined behavior. This can lead to unexpected results or program crashes on certain platforms.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
1U << 31
```
Reason:
By changing `1` to `1U`, the expression now uses an unsigned integer, which is well-defined when shifted left by 31 bits. This avoids the undefined behavior associated with shifting a signed integer and ensures that the code behaves correctly across different platforms.
